Business goal: Let root admins inspect the effective auth policy for any target tenant.
User outcome: A root admin can inspect any tenant's effective auth policy so platform operators can support customer-specific requirements and validate the live policy posture.
Notes / constraints: This is the root-only read seam for system defaults plus tenant overrides. Phase one must expose password-policy fields, session-expiry fields, and remediation-relevant effective rules. The same read model should leave room for future auth-method mode such as password_only and sso_only without changing the route shape.
Tenant context rule: root route path targets one explicit tenantId and runs outside tenant-auth tenant context
Explicitly denied roles: tenant admins; tenant users; unauthenticated callers
Authorization summary: Root admins may read any target tenant auth policy through a root-operated exact-tenant route. Tenant actors may not use this capability.
Frontend visibility rule: Future root-admin settings screens and support tooling may render the effective policy read-only or alongside edit controls.
Backend enforcement rule: Derive one effective policy from system defaults plus tenant overrides and enforce exact target-tenant visibility on the root route only.
Frontend surface: Future root-admin tenant auth policy viewer
Frontend states: loading, loaded, unauthorized, tenant not found, session expired
Session / expiry behavior: Read-only capability. Root-session reads follow normal root session expiry rules.
Client-side permission behavior: Client must treat returned effective policy as authoritative and must not compose fallback rules from cached defaults.
Request contract: No body. Exact tenantId param required. No client-supplied system-managed fields.
Response contract: Returns effective tenant auth policy with tenantId, policy source summary, password-policy fields, sessionPolicy, hard platform floors, hard session limits, updatedAt, and later-compatible authMethodMode field when introduced.
Error contract: 400 invalid tenantId; 401 unauthenticated; 403 unauthorized; 404 tenant not found or deleted.
Cross-feature seams: Depends on tenants visible-tenant seam for target tenant existence and later root authorization seam for governing capability checks.
Persistence impact: Read durable tenant policy override row plus central defaults; no mutation.
Indexes / uniqueness: Unique one-row-per-tenant override ownership. Index on tenantId. Optional updatedAt index for operational review; no search index needed in phase one.
Search / filter model: Exact read only; no list or search in phase one.
Compatibility / migration notes: Keep the response family broad enough for future authMethodMode and provider metadata summaries without redesigning the contract.
Authorization enforcement layer: Root auth middleware plus feature-local exact target-tenant enforcement.
CSP / browser security impact: No special CSP impact beyond future root-admin settings screens.
Audit requirement: Audit denied reads and optionally successful reads if privileged policy inspection becomes compliance-relevant; successful update history remains mandatory even if successful reads stay optional.
Privacy / personal data impact: Moderate; reveals tenant security policy posture and tenant identifiers but not credentials.
Standards impact: OWASP ASVS authorization and secure configuration visibility relevance plus privacy review for tenant-scoped settings exposure.
Acceptance notes: The effective policy returned to root admins is authoritative for one target tenant and supports platform-operator review without blurring into tenant-scoped capabilities.

Business goal: Let tenant admins inspect the effective auth policy for their own current tenant only.
User outcome: A tenant admin can inspect their own current tenant's effective auth policy so tenant-facing settings views and password-creation forms can show the governing rules transparently.
Notes / constraints: This is the tenant-scoped read seam for effective tenant auth policy. Phase one must expose password-policy fields, session-expiry fields, and remediation-relevant effective rules. The same read model should leave room for future auth-method mode such as password_only and sso_only without changing the route shape.
Tenant context rule: tenant-admin route must resolve exactly one current tenant context server-side and must not accept cross-tenant body or route selection
Allowed root roles: RootUserAdmin only if a future support-as-tenant path is explicitly designed; not part of this capability
Explicitly denied roles: root users on the root route; tenant actors without the matching tenant-admin authorization in the current tenant; tenant actors outside the current tenant; unauthenticated callers
Authorization summary: Tenant admins may read only the effective auth policy for their own current tenant context. Authentication alone is not sufficient; the actor must also satisfy the tenant-admin authorization rule for the current tenant. No actor may infer or read another tenant's policy through mutable request data or route-supplied tenant selectors on this capability.
Frontend visibility rule: Future tenant-admin settings screens and password-creation forms should render the effective policy read-only in phase one.
Backend enforcement rule: Derive one effective policy from system defaults plus tenant overrides and enforce current-tenant self-scope through authenticated tenant session context plus matching tenant-admin authorization for that current tenant.
Session / expiry behavior: Read-only capability. Tenant-session reads follow normal expiry rules.
Client-side permission behavior: Client must treat returned effective policy as authoritative and must not compose its own fallback rules from cached defaults.
Request contract: No body. Tenant route relies on authenticated current tenant context only. No client-supplied tenantId or system-managed fields.
Response contract: Returns effective tenant auth policy with tenantId, policySource, hasTenantOverride, password-policy fields, sessionPolicy, hard platform floors, hard session limits, updatedAt, and later-compatible authMethodMode field when introduced.
Error contract: 401 unauthenticated; 403 cross-tenant or unauthorized policy read; 409 no current tenant context if the session has not resolved one.
Cross-feature seams: Depends on tenant-session current-tenant context and later tenant authorization seam for tenant-admin read enforcement. Frontend guidance later depends on this shape staying stable.
Persistence impact: Read durable tenant policy override row plus central defaults; no mutation.
Indexes / uniqueness: Unique one-row-per-tenant override ownership. Index on tenantId. No search index needed in phase one.
Search / filter model: Exact current-tenant self-read only; no list or search in phase one.
Session / auth dependency: Authenticated tenant session with validated current tenant context required.
Compatibility / migration notes: Keep the response family broad enough for future authMethodMode and provider metadata summaries without redesigning the contract.
Authentication requirement: Authenticated tenant session plus matching tenant-admin authorization in the current tenant required.
Authorization enforcement layer: Tenant-session middleware plus tenant authorization enforcement plus feature-local current-tenant enforcement.
CSP / browser security impact: No special CSP impact beyond future tenant-admin settings screens.
Audit requirement: Audit denied reads and optionally successful reads if tenant-facing policy visibility becomes compliance-relevant later.
Privacy / personal data impact: Moderate; reveals tenant security policy posture and tenant identifiers only to an actor already bound to that tenant.
Standards impact: OWASP ASVS authorization and secure configuration visibility relevance plus privacy review for tenant-scoped settings exposure.
Acceptance notes: The effective policy returned to tenant admins is authoritative for their own current tenant only and preserves a strong separation from root-operated policy inspection.

Business goal: Allow root admins to apply tenant-specific auth policy overrides on top of the system baseline.
User outcome: A root admin can tighten or relax tenant password requirements and tenant session expiry within approved platform bounds and save a durable tenant override that takes effect immediately for that tenant.
Notes / constraints: Phase one writes password-policy override fields plus sessionTtlSeconds. The persistence and contract should still leave room for later auth-method mode fields without changing the feature boundary. Demo and test tenants may later inherit simpler defaults, but root-managed overrides still apply through the same seam. No tenant-admin write path exists in phase one.
Tenant context rule: root operator acts on one explicit target tenantId route param outside tenant-auth tenant context
Explicitly denied roles: tenant admins; tenant users; unauthenticated callers; authenticated root users without the governing capability
Authorization summary: This is a root-operated tenant-management capability. Authentication alone is not sufficient; the caller must also satisfy the root-admin authorization rule for this capability. Tenant actors may not edit policy in phase one.
Frontend visibility rule: No tenant-side edit UI in phase one; root-admin UI may arrive later and should treat this route as the only write authority.
Backend enforcement rule: Validate requested override fields against hard platform floors and ceilings then persist exactly one override row per tenant with audit-visible before and after values. Do not allow clients to write system-managed fields.
Session / expiry behavior: Immediate effect after successful save. No draft or scheduled activation in phase one.
Client-side permission behavior: No client-side permission guesswork; save path is root-only and server-authoritative.
Request contract: Body may include nullable override fields for minLength maxLength minUppercase maxUppercase minLowercase maxLowercase minNumbers maxNumbers minSymbols maxSymbols and sessionTtlSeconds. Empty strings rejected. Client cannot supply audit fields, version fields, or effective computed values.
Response contract: Returns updated effective tenant auth policy plus policySource, hasTenantOverride, passwordPolicy, sessionPolicy, hard floors, hard limits, and updatedAt. Response should be stable enough for a future root-admin settings screen.
Error contract: 400 invalid bounds or unsupported fields; 401 unauthenticated; 403 unauthorized; 404 tenant not found or deleted; 409 invalid policy combination when aggregate mins exceed maxLength.
Cross-feature seams: Depends on tenants visible-tenant seam and future root authorization seam; TenantAuth later consumes the effective-policy resolver seam and not the raw override row.
Persistence impact: Insert or update one durable tenant auth policy override row and one durable audit record with actor role actor id tenantId before values after values and timestamp.
Indexes / uniqueness: Unique policy override row by tenantId. Index on tenantId plus updatedAt. Audit storage should index tenantId and occurredAt for later history reads.
Search / filter model: Exact mutation only; no search surface.
Compatibility / migration notes: Immediate-effect model in phase one. Future authMethodMode or provider-policy fields should fit the same family without requiring a new feature. Existing credentials are not invalidated in place; they may instead trigger remediation on the next successful login
Authentication requirement: and new sessions use the effective tenant TTL immediately.
Authorization enforcement layer: Authenticated root session plus matching root-admin authorization required.
CSP / browser security impact: Root auth middleware plus root authorization enforcement plus feature-local validation and exact target-tenant enforcement.
Audit requirement: No special browser impact for API-only slice; future root-admin UI should remain same-origin and reuse existing posture.
Privacy / personal data impact: Audit successful changes and denied attempts with before/after policy values and actor role captured explicitly.
Standards impact: Moderate; mutates tenant security posture and may affect later user remediation state.
PRD required?: OWASP ASVS secure configuration and authorization relevance; likely SSDF and standards review required because this changes tenant auth posture.
column65: Root admins can update tenant password-policy and session-expiry overrides within platform guardrails and the resulting effective policy becomes immediately available to readers and auth flows.

Business goal: Authenticate a tenant principal by valid current credentials and immediately determine whether tenant-policy remediation blocks normal access.
User outcome: A tenant principal who signs in with a valid email and password receives a truthful login workflow result: onboarding required, tenant selection required, remediation required, or authenticated ready for normal access.
Notes / constraints: This extends the existing tenant password login capability rather than inventing a separate auth path. A stricter tenant policy must not silently reject a previously valid password at the credential-check step. Instead the login succeeds at identity proof and then evaluates remediation requirements for the selected or resolved tenant context. Because different tenants may later use different auth methods, the response shape must leave room for future policy outcomes such as sso_only without redesign. Session expiry must also remain compatible with the shared-principal model by taking the shortest effective tenant TTL across accessible tenant contexts.
Tenant context rule: authenticate shared principal first; then resolve exactly one remediation-relevant tenant context through auto-selection or explicit selection workflow before normal tenant access continues
Allowed root roles: RootUserAdmin only for support investigation if a future explicit route is designed; no root write behavior in phase one
Minimum role required: Authenticated tenant principal using valid credentials
Explicitly denied roles: unauthenticated callers without valid credentials; principals without tenant access; principals attempting to bypass remediation gate
Authorization summary: Shared tenant-auth login remains identity-first. After credential verification the feature must evaluate the effective auth policy for the resolved tenant context and return an explicit workflow state when the password no longer meets current tenant rules. Normal protected tenant actions stay blocked until remediation completes.
Authz scope type: shared authentication state transition over one principal and one resolved tenant context
Frontend visibility rule: Future login UI must handle authenticated; selection-required; remediation-required; invalid-credentials; and onboarding-required states deterministically.
Backend enforcement rule: Verify credentials first; resolve accessible tenant contexts safely; evaluate effective tenant auth policy for the resolved tenant context; and if remediation is required create or return a remediation-gated session state rather than granting normal tenant access.
Frontend states: idle, submitting, invalid credentials, onboarding required, selection required, remediation required, authenticated
Session / expiry behavior: Creates or refreshes a server-backed tenant session. Session may enter remediation-required blocking state and remain valid only for remediation-safe routes until cleared or expired. New session expiry uses the shortest effective tenant session TTL across the principal's accessible tenant contexts at login time.
Client-side permission behavior: Client must treat the returned workflow state and remediation details as authoritative and must not unlock the tenant app shell until remediation is completed.
Request contract: Body includes email and password only. No client-supplied tenantId or remediation flags. If multiple tenant contexts exist the response may require explicit selection before remediation can be evaluated for one current tenant context.
Response contract: Returns `200` with one explicit workflow state such as `INVALID_CREDENTIALS`, `ONBOARDING_REQUIRED`, `SELECTION_REQUIRED`, `REMEDIATION_REQUIRED`, or `AUTHENTICATED`. When remediation is required, the response includes session state plus remediation summary and the allowed next actions; session timestamps continue to expose the computed expiresAt value.
Error contract: 400 invalid payload; invalid-credential semantics should remain in the approved login state model rather than pretending remediation is a failed credential check; 403 no tenant access only when credentials are valid but the principal has no accessible tenant contexts.
Feature seam(s): tenantAuth login seam plus remediation-gate seam
Cross-feature seams: Depends on tenantConfiguration effective-policy resolver seam and on tenants plus tenant-access linkage. Must remain compatible with future SSO-only tenants and future tenant-admin or tenant-user actor types.
Persistence impact: Persist remediation-required session state or equivalent durable session flags tied to the current tenant context and remediation reason. Write audit evidence for remediation-triggering logins.
Indexes / uniqueness: Indexes on sessionId principalId activeTenantId remediationRequired and expiresAt. Principal-to-tenant linkage indexes remain required for tenant resolution.
Search / filter model: Exact login only; no search surface.
Session / auth dependency: No existing authenticated session required. Valid current credentials required.
Compatibility / migration notes: Supports future split between password_only and sso_only tenant modes. Password remediation is phase one; future non-password remediation reasons must fit the same response family.
Authentication requirement: No active session required; valid principal credentials required.
Authorization enforcement layer: Public auth middleware plus feature-local credential verification tenant-context resolution and remediation gating.
CSP / browser security impact: Frontend-facing login route should stay stable for later browser or app clients; no special CSP impact beyond existing frontend posture.
Audit requirement: Audit successful logins; denied attempts; and remediation-triggered logins with tenantId when known and outcome reason.
Privacy / personal data impact: High; handles credentials identity state tenant context resolution remediation blockers and session expiry posture.
Standards impact: OWASP ASVS authentication session-management and secure configuration controls; standards review strongly recommended because auth behavior changes.
Acceptance notes: Valid current credentials can produce a remediation-required workflow result that is explicit tenant-aware and blocking without being mislabeled as a failed login.

Business goal: Let an authenticated remediation-gated tenant principal or the frontend read exactly what must be fixed before normal access is restored.
User outcome: A signed-in tenant principal who is blocked by policy can see the remediation reason the governing tenant the effective password requirements and the next allowed action without guessing.
Notes / constraints: Phase one remediation type is password-policy remediation only, but the read model should leave room for future remediation types such as sso_required or mfa_enrollment_required. This capability should exist both as a dedicated route and as remediation summary data on login/session responses so the workflow remains explicit and frontend-friendly.
Tenant context rule: requires exactly one current tenant context on the authenticated remediation-gated session and returns only that tenant's remediation state
Explicitly denied roles: unauthenticated callers; authenticated sessions for other principals; principals attempting to read remediation state for another tenant
Authorization summary: This is a tenant-scoped self-read capability. Authentication alone is not sufficient; the actor must also be the same authenticated principal that owns the remediation-gated session in the current tenant context. The actor may read only their own current remediation state for their own authenticated session and current tenant context.
Authz scope type: self read over current remediation-gated session
Frontend visibility rule: Future frontend remediation screen depends on this to render exact guidance and validation hints.
Backend enforcement rule: Enforce current remediation-gated session ownership and return the current tenant's remediation state only. Do not accept mutable tenant selectors or principal identifiers from the client.
Frontend states: loading, remediation required, remediation cleared, session expired
Session / expiry behavior: Read-only on the existing remediation-gated session. If the session expires the actor must authenticate again before continuing remediation.
Client-side permission behavior: Client should treat returned remediation details and policy rules as authoritative and should not infer from stale cached policy data alone.
Request contract: No body. Authenticated remediation-gated tenant session required.
Response contract: Returns remediationRequired, remediationReason, tenant summary, effective password-policy requirements, allowed next actions, and whether any normal app access remains blocked. The same core remediation summary should also be reusable inside login and current-session responses.
Error contract: 401 invalid or expired session; 403 session not in a remediation-readable state or not owned by the current actor.
Cross-feature seams: Depends on tenantConfiguration effective-policy resolver seam and on current tenant-session context. May later share shape with session-read responses.
Persistence impact: Read remediation-gated session state and effective tenant auth policy; no mutation.
Indexes / uniqueness: Indexes on sessionId principalId activeTenantId remediationRequired. No search surface.
Compatibility / migration notes: Keep the response family broad enough for later non-password remediation reasons without changing route semantics.
Authentication requirement: Authenticated remediation-gated tenant session plus self-ownership of the remediation state required.
Authorization enforcement layer: Tenant-session middleware plus self-ownership enforcement plus feature-local remediation-state enforcement.
CSP / browser security impact: Frontend-ready blocker route with no special CSP requirement beyond future browser compatibility.
Audit requirement: Audit denied reads; successful remediation-state reads may stay optional if successful session bootstrap already captures the same visibility event.
Privacy / personal data impact: Moderate; exposes tenant and policy metadata only to the affected authenticated actor.
Standards impact: OWASP ASVS session-management and user-guidance relevance for secure remediation workflows.
Acceptance notes: An affected tenant principal can read exactly why access is blocked and which policy-compliant next step is required through both dedicated remediation reads and the broader auth/session workflow surfaces.

Business goal: Allow a remediation-gated tenant principal to set a new password that satisfies the current tenant policy and then unlock normal access.
User outcome: A tenant principal who authenticated successfully but was blocked by stronger tenant policy can change their password within the same remediation workflow and then continue into normal tenant access once the new password is accepted.
Notes / constraints: Phase one completes password-policy remediation only. This is not a general support override and must not bypass the tenant's effective policy. The route should reuse shared credential ownership and hashing rules while remaining tenant-policy aware. Successful completion clears the remediation gate for the current tenant context and should also support future frontend guidance flows. When the principal has access to multiple tenants, tenant-selection capability must remain available on a remediation-gated session until one current tenant context is established.
Tenant context rule: requires exactly one current tenant context on a remediation-gated authenticated session and clears remediation only for the current authenticated principal and current tenant context
Explicitly denied roles: unauthenticated callers; principals not in remediation-required state; actors attempting to remediate another principal or another tenant
Authorization summary: This is a tenant-scoped self-remediation capability. Authentication alone is not sufficient; the actor must also own the remediation-gated session and current tenant context being remediated. The actor may change only their own password and only through their authenticated remediation-gated session. Root admins do not bypass the policy through this route.
Authz scope type: self remediation mutation over current principal and current tenant
Frontend visibility rule: Future remediation blocker screen must submit to this route and render exact validation errors from the effective tenant policy.
Backend enforcement rule: Enforce current remediation-gated session ownership; validate the new password against the effective tenant policy and platform floors; update the shared principal credential; clear the remediation gate; refresh the session state; and keep normal tenant access blocked if remediation fails.
Frontend states: idle, submitting, validation errors, remediation cleared, session expired
Session / expiry behavior: Uses the existing remediation-gated session. On success the same session may transition to normal authenticated state for the current tenant if no further remediation remains.
Client-side permission behavior: Client must not assume local password validation is sufficient; server validation against effective tenant policy remains authoritative.
Request contract: Body includes currentPassword when required by the final contract plus newPassword and repeatPassword. No client-supplied policy fields tenantId or principalId. System-managed session and audit fields are server-owned.
Response contract: Returns updated session/auth state with remediationRequired=false when successful plus effective current tenant context and next-step guidance.
Error contract: 400 invalid payload or policy violation with exact corrective reasons; 401 invalid or expired session; 403 session not eligible for remediation completion or not owned by the current actor; 409 remediation state changed or password reuse/conflict if the final contract distinguishes those cases.
Cross-feature seams: Depends on tenantConfiguration effective-policy resolver seam and shared credential storage in tenantAuth. Must remain compatible with future password reset and future non-password remediation workflows.
Persistence impact: Update durable password credential; remediation-gated session state; session timestamps; and audit records. May persist password-changed-at or remediation-cleared-at metadata if added later.
Indexes / uniqueness: Indexes on principal credential ownership plus session remediation state. Existing credential uniqueness and session indexes remain required.
Compatibility / migration notes: No support bypass in phase one. Future password reset and future non-password remediation should reuse the same state-machine concepts without rewriting the auth model. Multi-tenant principals must still be allowed to complete tenant selection while remediation-gated so one current tenant context can be established before remediation completion.
Authentication requirement: Authenticated remediation-gated tenant session plus self-ownership of the remediation state required.
Authorization enforcement layer: Tenant-session middleware plus self-ownership enforcement plus feature-local remediation-state enforcement and policy validation.
CSP / browser security impact: Frontend-ready remediation route with no special CSP impact beyond future browser compatibility.
Audit requirement: Audit successful remediation completion and denied attempts with principalId tenantId previous reason and outcome captured explicitly.
Privacy / personal data impact: High; handles credential rotation under a policy-enforcement workflow and affects tenant access state.
Standards impact: OWASP ASVS authentication credential-management and remediation-flow controls; strong standards review recommended.
Acceptance notes: A remediation-gated actor can set a policy-compliant password and regain normal access without any policy-bypass path.
